summary: The article provides a largely accurate and comprehensive overview of ESOP taxation in India, covering both perquisite and capital gains aspects, with good detail on holding periods and ITR forms. However, some specific tax rates and holding periods for listed shares, particularly STCG, appear to be outdated or incorrect based on recent amendments.

claims.claim: The moment you exercise your ESOPs, the benefit you receive is treated as a "perquisite" and is taxable as salary income under the head "Salaries" as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: This is accurate. The perquisite value is taxable under Section 17(2)(vi) of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: For unlisted shares, the FMV is determined by a SEBI-registered merchant banker as per Rule 3(8) of the Income Tax Rules.
claims.note: Rule 3(8) and Rule 3(9) of the Income Tax Rules prescribe the method for determining Fair Market Value of shares on the exercise date for listed and unlisted companies respectively. For unlisted shares, FMV is determined by a SEBI-registered merchant banker.

claims.claim: For unlisted company ESOPs, the Income Tax Act provides for deferment of TDS on perquisite income to the earlier of: 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, date of sale of shares, or date of cessation of employment.
claims.note: This is accurate for eligible startups. The deferment is allowed for 48 months from the end of the assessment year in which securities are allotted, or the date of sale of shares, or the date the employee ceases to be an employee, whichever is earliest.

claims.claim: Listed Shares: Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG): If held for 12 months or less. Taxed at 15% (plus cess and surcharge) if Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is paid.
claims.note: For listed equity shares where STT is paid, STCG (held for 12 months or less) is taxed at 20% (plus cess and surcharge) for transfers made on or after July 23, 2024.

claims.claim: Listed Shares: Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG): If held for more than 12 months. Taxed at 10% (plus cess and surcharge) on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year, if STT is paid. Gains up to ₹1 lakh are exempt.
claims.note: For listed shares held for more than 12 months, LTCG is taxed at 12.5% (plus cess and surcharge) on gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh, effective from July 23, 2024.

claims.claim: Unlisted Shares: Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG): If held for 24 months or less. Taxed at your applicable income tax slab rates.
claims.note: This is correct. STCG on unlisted shares (held for 24 months or less) is added to total income and taxed at the individual's applicable slab rates.

claims.claim: Unlisted Shares: Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG): If held for more than 24 months. Taxed at 20% (plus cess and surcharge) with the benefit of indexation.
claims.note: For unlisted shares held for more than 24 months, LTCG is taxed at 12.5% (plus cess and surcharge) without indexation benefit for transfers made on or after July 23, 2024.

claims.claim: ITR-1 (Sahaj): Not suitable if you have capital gains from ESOPs.
claims.note: ITR-1 is not suitable for individuals with capital gains (other than certain limited LTCG under Section 112A up to ₹1.25 lakh).

article_title: ESOP Tax Rules for ITR: Navigating Salary & Capital Gains
